pr_title: BUG: Fix regression on DataFrame.replace for regex
pr_body:
The commit ensures that the replacement for regex is not confined to the 
beginning of the string but spans all the characters within. The 
behaviour is then consistent with versions prior to 0.24.0.

- [x] closes #25259
- [x] tests added / passed
- [ ] passes `git diff upstream/master -u -- "*.py" | flake8 --diff`
- [x] whatsnew entry
pr_comments:
this seems highly related to https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/24804 and a corresponding PR #24935 

can you have a look
i just took a quick look... seems the problems don't look the same... shall i move whatsnew in my PR to 0.24.2 from 0.25? @jreback

@jreback and @charlesdong1991 Hi, thanks for taking a look at this. I have very little knowledge about `pandas` internals but, from the description of #24804, it does not seem to be the same problem. I will try to include a test specifically for the case where the regex pattern is inside the string and not at the beginning. The current change already passes all the tests in `tests/frame/test_replace.py`.

``` python3
# add this to the start of to_replace: r"(.*?)"
# add this to the start of replacement value: r"\1"

```

issue_context.title: replace method with comma separator does not work in pandas 0.24.1
issue_context.body:
### The latest version (0.24.1) does not replace comma separator, but 0.23.4 does.

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({'one': ["1,000", "2,000"], 'two': ["3,000", "4,000"]})
df = df.replace({',': ''}, regex=True)

print(pd.__version__)
print(df)
```

```
0.23.4
    one   two
0  1000  3000
1  2000  4000
```

```
0.24.1
     one    two
0  1,000  3,000
1  2,000  4,000
```

If other characters are used with a comma, it works normally
```
df = df.replace({'1,': ''}, regex=True)
```
```
     one    two
0    000  3,000
1  2,000  4,000
```
comments:
Hi, it is not related to commas. In your example @mr-yoo, if you try to replace `,0`, it also fails. The replacement works only if the pattern is the beginning of the string
```
df.replace({',0': ''}, regex=True)
```

```
0.23.4
   one  two
0  100  300
1  200  400
```

```
0.24.1
     one    two
0  1, 000  3,000
1  2,000  4,000
```

Can it be related to
```
op = np.vectorize(lambda x: bool(re.match(b, x)) if isinstance(x, str)
                  else False)
``` 
in managers.py? 

`re.match` checks only if the beginning of the string matches. Should it be `re.search`? From my tests, it seems to reproduce the previous behaviour.

@PetitLepton seems logical, so maybe introduced as part of https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/20656

Would certainly welcome a PR to fix if you are up for one

review_comments: Since we moved from `match` to `search` here can you also updated the function name?
